core_obligations: Reduce to the Noetherian case (proof lines 12104-12114): part (2) implies part (1) by taking the disjoint union of the pieces; writing the rings as filtered colimits of finite type algebras over the integers and descending the finitely presented algebra, quasi-finiteness descends, so it suffices to treat finite type algebras over the integers; the author records that the details of this reduction are omitted.

Reduce to the finite case (proof lines 12117-12125): over a Noetherian base, generic finiteness and Noetherian induction give a finite partition into locally closed strata over which the morphism is finite, which may be refined to affine strata.

Reduce to the model case (proof lines 12127-12164): it suffices to prove the result after a surjective flat quasi-finite base change; then applying the structure result for finite morphisms the author assumes the target is a set theoretic union of closed subschemes mapping isomorphically to the base, and a final partition makes their mutual intersections trivial, which exhibits the desired decomposition.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to finite type algebras over the integers using descent of quasi-finiteness.
In the Noetherian case produce a partition on which the morphism is finite, and reduce to the finite case.
Use the structure of finite morphisms to reach the model case and conclude by a suitable partition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma decomposes a quasi-finite finitely presented morphism of affine schemes: after a surjective morphism of affine bases it becomes a thickening of a finite etale morphism, and a finite partition of the base by locally closed affine strata together with finite locally free covers realizes the morphism as a finite disjoint union of copies of the strata after reduction (statement lines 12084-12101). The proof is a long sequence of reductions: it descends to finite type algebras over the integers, that is, to the Noetherian case (proof lines 12104-12114); it uses generic finiteness and Noetherian induction to reach the finite case (proof lines 12117-12125); and it then shows that a surjective flat quasi-finite base change suffices and reduces to the model in which the morphism is a finite union of closed subschemes mapping isomorphically, a final partition completing the construction (proof lines 12127-12164). The non-formal content is the chain of reductions and the model case. The claim is H2: a structured reduction whose inputs are named.
